market.category: NFL advanced player analytics and comparison apps
market.audience: NFL fans, fantasy and dynasty players, writers, and creators who need fast context on a player's value
market.problem: Box scores tell fans what happened, but not who was efficient, who is changing, or how a favorite fits the league
market.advantage: Football Next: StatScout turns advanced NFL metrics into scannable leaderboards, player profiles, recent movement, team context, following shortcuts, and side-by-side comparisons
market.competitive_context: It competes with score apps and dense desktop analytics pages. It wins by making EPA, percentile context, recent form, and fan-selected players readable in one mobile workflow

proof_points.claim: The Stats screen ranks fictional qualified quarterbacks by Pass Yds with visible position, season, metric, and sort controls
The player profile shows advanced percentile bars and the metric values behind a quarterback's ranking
The Trends screen surfaces quarterback movement with an honest week boundary and a selected recent window
The Chiefs team page keeps team context and roster paths in one real navigation destination
The Following board keeps a fan's team and selected players one tap away with season summaries
The player comparison screen aligns two quarterbacks and their season totals for a clear debate
The year comparison screen puts two available seasons into one metric-by-metric view

story.throughline: Move from a quick league scan to the context, movement, team view, and fan shortcuts that make every football debate easier

pitch.benefit: Find the players creating the most value without leaving the league board
pitch.problem: Box-score leaderboards hide efficiency and make advanced research slow
pitch.advantage: StatScout ranks qualified players with familiar production and a path to advanced context
pitch.proof: The literal Stats capture shows qualified quarterbacks ranked by Pass Yds with season, position, stat, and sort controls visible
